item.content:encoded:
Defence and International Security

发布源: 36. Casimir Pulaski Foundation --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-08-04

The Pulaski Foundation Defence and Security Program provides multidisciplinary analysis of the current and emerging defense and security challenges facing the Transatlantic Alliance – with a special focus on Central and Eastern Europe.

Since 2022 the program allocates much of its resources to analysing the possible outcomes and consequences for European security of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. A special component of the program is devoted to the challenges and opportunities facing Poland’s defense policy, including modernizing of the Polish army and its industry. The main goal is to present actionable recommendations to an array of Polish stakeholders, including public administration, which could form a basis for long-term strategies for Poland in times of raising military and defense demands.

Overall, through its analysis, the program advocates for a stronger presence of NATO on the Alliance’s Eastern Flank, more developed European defence capabilities and argues for the need to provide military assistance and solid security guarantees to Ukraine.

item.content:encoded:
Ukrainian attacks on Russian logistics hubs. Day 1616 of the war

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-08-04

The change of Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine came at a time of intense Russian military pressure on several fronts(see: ‘Change of commander-in-chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine’). Russian forces continued their operations near Dobropillia, Kostiantynivka and Lyman, while Ukrainian troops counterattacked in the Novopavlivka and Novooleksandrivka directions.

The situation is most difficult in and around Kostiantynivka. Fighting continues in the northern part of the urban area, where isolated pockets of Ukrainian resistance reportedly remain. Meanwhile, Russian assault groups are becoming increasingly active in Oleksiievo-Druzhkivka, north-west of the city. The position of Ukrainian forces across this entire sector continues to deteriorate, particularly as Russian troops are seeking to sever logistics routes north of Kostiantynivka.

Ukrainian counterattacks in the Novopavlivka and Novooleksandrivka directions have produced some local gains, but have failed to break through the Russian force grouping.According to Ukrainian sources, Russian troops have been pushed back near the village of Filiia and Ukrainian units have been advancing slowly in sectors between the Yanchur, Vorona and Vovcha rivers, reportedly aiming to move closer to the Huliaipole–Velyka Novosilka road. These operations have forced Russian units to undertake stabilisation efforts, but Ukrainian troops have yet to achieve their objective of directly threatening Russia’s supply system.

item.content:encoded:
Russia: The Kremlin strips political exiles of their civil rights

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-08-04

On 22–24 July, the Russian parliament unanimously adopted a package of laws that drastically curtails the civil rights of Russian citizens living abroad. The measures target those who have been convicted in criminal or administrative cases and are deemed to be ‘evading punishment’. According to the text of the legislation and statements by government officials, the measures are aimed primarily at those who have fled abroad to escape political repression. Those affected will be entered into a special register maintained by Russia’s Ministry of Justice. The new provisions will enter into force immediately after they are signed by Vladimir Putin.

The restrictions apply to several categories of political exiles. These include people convicted of serious offences, including extremism, terrorism and treason. Such charges are increasingly used to punish political activity. The measures also cover so-called ‘foreign agents’ (individuals and legal entities designated by the Russian authorities as being ‘under foreign influence’; more than 1,200 entities currently hold this status) and people convicted of involvement in the activities of an ‘undesirable organisation’ (a designation applied to more than 380 foreign organisations deemed to threaten Russia’s security).
